Command: A man who violates a virgin shall marry her
Summary: Deuteronomy 22:28-29 requires a man who lays hold on an unbetrothed virgin to marry her and pay her father fifty shekels of silver. The wrong is answered with lifelong responsibility and payment.
Commandment: A man who violates a virgin shall marry her and pay the bride-price.
Application: Debated: how far these civil remedies carry into the church is genuinely disputed, and the remedy itself raises hard questions today — this row does not settle them. The principle aimed at — the wrongdoer bears the cost, not the victim alone — endures.
Purpose: To protect the weaker party at each family step (Deuteronomy 21-25). Debated: the divorce certificate is read by Jesus as concession to hardness of heart, not God's design (Matthew 19:8), and levirate marriage ended, while creation marriage itself is reaffirmed. The site does not settle a single duration for this cluster because its parts do not share one fate.
